why: Found while building, on the planted fixture, before any measured run. P3's claim enumerates its inputs (S1: every slice of length 0 to 3 over the element type's edge values; S2: every array whose read bytes are set from {0, 1, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xff} at up to two iterations) and predicts at least 2000 cases; that enumeration gives 1690 (an arithmetic error in the prereg), so the count misses. The test asserted the count before comparing, so the miss would also hide the differential check itself. It is split, with no assertion weakened: test_p3_model_equals_go keeps the comparison (real Go = compiled model = the shapes' mirror on every enumerated case: 1690 of 1690 agree locally), and test_p3_case_count keeps the count assertion unchanged (at least 2000; P3's recorded miss, 1690, scored as missed in docs/iterations/I122.md and left out of the CI job as I104's and I108's recorded misses are). The inputs are exactly the claim's; none is added.

Found while building, on the planted fixture, before any measured run. P4 states Signed's witness as s = [-101]; the planted run refutes Signed's totality at s = [-128] (the smallest sample that panics: -128 < -100 holds, and the witness replays as real Go), so the stated witness misses. The test asserted it before the replay, so the miss would also hide the replay of every REFUTED witness. It is split, with no assertion weakened: test_p4_false_laws_refuted_and_replayed keeps every other assertion (the four laws REFUTED, the three other witnesses, every REFUTED witness replayed as real Go), and test_p4_signed_witness keeps the [-101] assertion unchanged (P4's recorded miss, scored in docs/iterations/I122.md and left out of the CI job).

Found after both measured runs (baseline and counted, Q104), when scoring. The test compared the corpus summary's laws_derived, laws_decided and bind_bound, but the run's summary carries none of these keys, so the comparison was None == None and vacuous: it could not miss. The law counts a composed run commits are the rows' laws_aggregate (derived, decided, unknown per family; I118, I120). The test now reads them: the laws decided (PROVED and REFUTED together, Q56) summed over the rows, and the ops in S1 or S2, as before. It is split, with no assertion weakened: the PAR comparison is test_p9_par_laws_equal_baseline. Nothing is added to the claim, and its inputs are the two committed runs.

Split from test_p9_ops_in_class_and_laws, after both measured runs, when the vacuous comparison was found (that line). It asserts P9's PAR claim as stated: per entry and PAR family, the PAR laws derived in the counted run equal the baseline's (laws_aggregate). It misses: the baseline did not extract the Go documents of two entries (a network refusal from the module checksum database, and packages that did not load), which the counted run extracted, so the counted run has 29 more PAR laws (all UNKNOWN), and 268 laws derived equals I120's committed corpus run. This is P9's recorded miss, scored in docs/iterations/I122.md with that cause; it is reported, never forced. No run is repeated (Q80).
